The effect of anxiety on wellbeing is significant where support is from 2.19 upward, and not significant elsewhere in the observed range (0.88 to 7.87). These cut-offs are the Johnson-Neyman points. The interaction p-value is the test of whether the slope changes with support; the simple slopes describe the shape. A significant interaction does not show that support causes the change. 3 rows were left out because a value was missing.

Assumption checks

VariableNShapiro-Wilk Wp
Residuals570.972.205

No Shapiro-Wilk p is below .05, so nothing here argues against normality. That is weaker evidence than it sounds when groups are small.

3 entries that are not a number were left out.

A moderation analysis showed that support significantly moderated the effect of anxiety on wellbeing, b = 0.08, SE = 0.02, t(53) = 3.64, p < .001, ΔR² = .073. The simple slope of anxiety was 0.25 (p < .001), 0.40 (p < .001), 0.55 (p < .001) at low, average and high support (mean − 1 SD, mean, mean + 1 SD). Predictors were mean-centred.
